newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex says substandard part contributed to blaze.
newsitem.headline: Pemex says substandard part contributed to blaze.

text.p: Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) chairman Adrian Lajous told legislators Tuesday that substandard equipment may have contributed to last week's blaze at a gasoline storage facility belonging to the state-owned oil and gas monopoly in northern Mexico City.

"In preliminary conclusions it has been established that the primary cause of the accident was a fault in the H-8 valve," Lajous said. "This valve does not comply with actual requirements and, apparently, not with those prevailing when it was installed."

On November 11 three gas tanks at the storage center caught fire, killing three Pemex workers and a fireman and leaving 15 others burned and hospitalized. The blaze sent smoke three miles into the air, visible throughout the nation's capital, and required more than 600 firefighters and 36 hours to extinguish it.
The Pemex chair detailed preliminary findings from studies of the blast to legislators, who responded with barbed questions and suspicions from across the political spectrum.
"What other unsecure conditions exist, undetected in the petroleum industry?" asked Jorge Wade Gonzalez, a deputy with the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party.
Lawmakers also recalled two other accidents in the past three years at Pemex installations, and questioned previous efforts to better check equipment.
In response to legislators' doubts, Lajous repeated his intent to boost security and training and improve technology throughout Pemex installations.
"We need to dramatically modify operating discipline at every Pemex work site," Lajous said. "I believe we have suffered enough accidents to justify a radical strategy change."
Lajous insisted the problem did not stem from a lack of maintenance spending, and said the company and state technicians would continue studying the causes of the blast.
